items.help: Group id (gid) whose members may also use the admin socket, e.g. 1000; -1 (default) allows only root and the server's own user.
items.label: Admin socket group (gid)

items.help: Path of the local socket of the `kudurru admin` command (reset-password, create-token, list-users), e.g. /run/kudurru/kudurru.sock: the way back in when every admin password is lost. Only uid 0, the server's own user and auth.adminSocket.group may use it. Empty turns it off.
items.label: Admin socket path

items.help: Path of a file holding the password of the first admin account, created on the first start, e.g. /run/secrets/kudurru-admin-password. The KUDURRU_ADMIN_PASSWORD and KUDURRU_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE environment variables take precedence; with none of them, a password is generated and printed once.
items.label: First-boot admin password file

items.help: Sign-in to the dashboard through an OpenID Connect provider such as Google, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, Authentik or Dex; the provider's ID tokens also work as bearer tokens for the API. Each entry needs an id, issuer, clientID, clientSecretFile and redirectURL; scopes, claimValidationRules, claimMappings and provisioning are optional.
items.label: Identity providers

fields.name: id
fields.label: ID
fields.help: Short name of the provider, a lowercase DNS label such as corp. It appears in the login URLs and, as corp:, in front of every username and group from this provider.

fields.name: displayName
fields.label: Display name
fields.help: Name on the login button, e.g. Company SSO; empty shows the id.

fields.name: issuer
fields.label: Issuer
fields.help: Issuer URL of the OpenID Provider exactly as it publishes it, e.g. https://accounts.google.com or https://sso.home.example/realms/home; https is required except on loopback.

fields.name: clientID
fields.label: Client ID
fields.help: Client ID of the web application registered for kudurru at the provider.

fields.name: clientSecretFile
fields.label: Client secret file
fields.help: Path of a file holding the client secret of clientID, e.g. /etc/kudurru/oidc-secret; required, because kudurru signs in as a confidential client.

fields.name: cliClientID
fields.label: CLI client ID
fields.help: Public client ID for signing in from the command line (kudurru login, v0.2); ID tokens issued to it are accepted as bearer tokens. Empty for none.

fields.name: redirectURL
fields.label: Redirect URL
fields.help: Callback URL registered at the provider: the dashboard URL followed by /api/v1/auth/oidc/<id>/callback, e.g. https://dns.home.example/api/v1/auth/oidc/corp/callback.

fields.name: scopes
fields.label: Scopes
fields.help: Scopes requested at sign-in; empty requests openid, profile, email and groups. openid is always added.

fields.name: audiences
fields.label: Audiences
fields.help: Extra audience (aud) values accepted on bearer ID tokens from this provider; empty for none.

fields.name: claimValidationRules
fields.label: Claim validation rules
fields.help: Claims every sign-in must carry, as {claim, requiredValue} pairs, e.g. claim email_verified with requiredValue "true"; a sign-in that fails one is refused.

fields.name: claimMappings
fields.label: Claim mappings
fields.help: Which claims give the username, groups, display name and email: {username: {claim, prefix}, groups: {claim, prefix}, displayName: {claim}, email: {claim}}. Empty uses preferred_username (then upn, a verified email, sub), groups and roles, name and email; prefixes default to <id>:.

fields.name: provisioning
fields.label: Provisioning
fields.help: Who may sign in the first time, as {autoProvision, defaultRole}: mapped-only (default) admits only sign-ins a role binding matches; always admits everyone the provider vouches for; never admits only identities kudurru already knows. defaultRole (not admin) is granted to an admitted sign-in without a binding.

fields.name: allowedDomains
fields.label: Allowed email domains
fields.help: Reserved: email domains sign-ins will be restricted to, e.g. home.example. Accepted but not enforced yet.

items.help: How Kubernetes service-account tokens are authorized: sar asks the apiserver with a SubjectAccessReview on kudurru.io resources. impersonate is planned for v0.2.
items.label: Kubernetes authorization

enum.label: SubjectAccessReview
enum.help: Ask the apiserver with a SubjectAccessReview whether the service account may act on the kudurru.io resource.

items.help: Whether people can sign in to the dashboard with a username and password: enabled for everyone, admins-only for builtin admins, or disabled (identity providers only). `kudurru admin` on the server's admin socket always works, so you cannot lock yourself out. Gates POST /api/v1/auth/login.
items.label: Local password login

enum.label: Enabled
enum.help: Every local user may sign in with a password.

enum.label: Admins only
enum.help: Only builtin admins may sign in with a password; everyone else uses an identity provider.

enum.label: Disabled
enum.help: No password sign-in; use an identity provider. kudurru admin over the admin socket still works.

items.help: Sign a dashboard user out after this long without activity, e.g. 30m; at least 1m. Every request starts the time again.
items.label: Session idle timeout

items.help: Longest a dashboard sign-in lasts however active it is, e.g. 12h; then the user signs in again and their roles are looked up afresh. At least auth.session.idleTimeout.
items.label: Session lifetime

items.help: Whether browsers send the session cookie only over HTTPS (the cookie's Secure attribute). auto (default) decides per request and suits most setups; always is for a proxy that terminates TLS without telling kudurru; never is only for plain HTTP on a network you trust.
items.label: Secure session cookie

enum.label: Auto
enum.help: Secure when TLS terminates at kudurru or a trusted proxy reports https.

enum.label: Always
enum.help: Always Secure; for a proxy that terminates TLS without sending X-Forwarded-Proto.

enum.label: Never
enum.help: Never Secure: for plain HTTP only, and the cookie can be read on the network.

items.help: Longest lifetime of a new API token, e.g. 2160h (90 days); a token created without an expiry gets this one. 0 (default) allows tokens that never expire.
items.label: Maximum token lifetime

items.help: How people reach you, shown as "Ask your administrator": an email address, e.g. admin@home.example, or a link, e.g. https://wiki.home.example/dns. Empty leaves the line out.
items.label: Administrator contact

items.help: Address of the dashboard the block page links administrators to, e.g. https://192.168.1.10:8080; the link opens /queries?domain=... there. Empty builds it from the block page address and listeners.api; set it when the dashboard is reached under another name or through a reverse proxy.
items.label: Dashboard URL

items.help: Show browsers a page that explains why a site was blocked, instead of a connection error. Turning it on starts the block page listener (listeners.blockPage) and allows the blockPage block response; choose that response in blocking.defaultResponse or a Policy. Blocked A and AAAA queries then point at blockPage.ipv4 and blockPage.ipv6; other types get NODATA.
items.label: Block page enabled

items.help: Address browsers are sent to for the block page, e.g. 192.168.1.10: this server's LAN address, or a VIP or load balancer in front of the block page. Blocked A queries are answered with it under the blockPage response. Empty picks the first specific address of listeners.blockPage, else of listeners.dns; when every listener binds all addresses (0.0.0.0, ::) there is none, and blockPage.enabled is refused.
items.label: Block page IPv4 address

items.help: IPv6 address browsers are sent to for the block page, e.g. fd00::10; blocked AAAA queries are answered with it under the blockPage response. When blockPage.ipv4 is empty too, one is picked from the listeners as for IPv4; without an IPv6 address, AAAA queries get NODATA and browsers use IPv4.
items.label: Block page IPv6 address

items.default: The administrator of this network has blocked access to this domain.
items.help: Text under the heading that tells people why the site is blocked and what they can do (plain text, at most 2000 characters; HTML is shown as text).
items.label: Page message

items.help: Most block page requests one client address may make per minute, e.g. 120, with bursts up to the same number; beyond it the page answers 429 Too Many Requests. 0 removes the limit.
items.label: Requests per minute per client

items.help: Show what blocked the name (the list, rule, blocked service, safe search or policy), looked up in the recent query log. Off shows only the domain, the client, the node and the time, which keeps your list choices private.
items.label: Show block details

items.help: Heading of the block page, e.g. This site is blocked (plain text, at most 200 characters).
items.label: Page title

items.help: Answer queries and report ready while blocklists are still loading, e.g. right after a restart; queries are filtered by the lists already loaded. Off, the node reports not ready until every referenced list is loaded, so load balancers keep traffic away.
items.label: Serve while lists load

items.help: Allow blocklist URLs that point at this machine or at special addresses: loopback, link-local (169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10, where cloud metadata services live), unspecified and multicast. Off by default so whoever can add a BlockList cannot make the node fetch internal services (SSRF). Lists on private LAN addresses such as 192.168.1.5 are always allowed.
items.label: Allow local list URLs

items.help: How long devices may remember a block answer, e.g. 10m, unless the Policy sets blockTTL. Keep it short: after you allow a name, devices keep the cached block until it expires.
items.label: Block response TTL

items.help: Off when empty. Opt-in: a URL of AdGuard's HostlistsRegistry blocked-services file, e.g. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdguardTeam/HostlistsRegistry/main/assets/services.json, adds its services (about 140) to the catalogue next to kudurru's own; kudurru's entries win when both have an ID. That data is GPL-3.0 licensed: kudurru does not ship it, your instance downloads it (the leader, on the catalogue refresh interval; the other nodes copy the leader's), and the dashboard marks those services as from AdGuard (GPL-3.0). Check that the licence suits how you use and share the data. docs/deploy/blocked-services.md.
items.label: AdGuard services URL (GPL-3.0, opt-in)

items.help: How often the catalogue at blocking.catalogue.url and the AdGuard services at blocking.catalogue.adguardServicesURL are checked for a new version, e.g. 24h; at least 1m. A conditional GET, so an unchanged document is not downloaded again.
items.label: Catalogue refresh interval

items.help: Leave empty to use the blocked-services and safe-search catalogue built into kudurru. A URL, e.g. https://example.com/kudurru-catalogue.json, replaces it with your own document (schema version 2, or 1, docs/deploy/blocked-services.md). The leader downloads it and the other nodes copy the leader's; a document that fails validation leaves the current catalogue in service.
items.label: Catalogue URL

items.help: IPv4 address blocked A queries are answered with when the block response is customIP, e.g. 192.168.1.10 for a server of yours that shows a notice. Empty answers NODATA.
items.label: Custom block IPv4

items.help: IPv6 address blocked AAAA queries are answered with when the block response is customIP, e.g. fd00::10. Empty answers NODATA.
items.label: Custom block IPv6

items.help: What a blocked query is answered with, unless the client's Policy (blockMode) or the BlockList (response) chooses otherwise. zeroIP (default) makes the connection fail at once and suits most networks; blockPage shows browsers a page that explains the block; refused is discouraged, because devices then ask another DNS server.
items.label: Default block response

enum.label: Zero IP
enum.help: Answer 0.0.0.0 (A) or :: (AAAA), so the connection fails at once; other record types get an empty answer (NODATA). Suits most networks.

enum.label: NXDOMAIN
enum.help: Answer that the name does not exist (NXDOMAIN), for every record type.

enum.label: Custom IP
enum.help: Answer the addresses in blocking.customIP.v4 and v6, e.g. a server of yours; a family without an address gets NODATA.

enum.label: REFUSED
enum.help: Refuse the query. Discouraged: most devices then ask their next DNS server, which bypasses blocking.

enum.label: Block page
enum.help: Send browsers to the block page, which explains why the name was blocked (needs blockPage.enabled); other record types get NODATA.

items.help: Block ads, trackers and other listed names for the whole network; off answers every query unfiltered. To pause blocking for a while, use the temporary disable on the dashboard instead (a runtime toggle, not this key). Applies to forwarded queries, not to your own zones.
items.label: Blocking enabled

items.help: What happens at start while blocklists load: fast (default) serves at once using the copies saved on disk; blocking waits until every list is loaded; failOnError also exits when a list cannot be loaded.
items.label: List loading at start

enum.label: Fast
enum.help: Serve at once using the lists saved on disk, and load fresh copies in the background.

enum.label: Wait for lists
enum.help: Report not ready until every list is loaded.

enum.label: Fail on error
enum.help: Wait for every list, and exit with an error when one fails to load.

items.help: Directory where downloaded blocklists are saved so the next start can use them at once. Empty uses <node.dataDir>/lists. Files are named by the sha256 of the list URL.
items.label: List cache directory

items.help: How often blocklists are downloaded again when a list sets no refreshInterval of its own, e.g. 24h; at least 1m. In a cluster the leader downloads and the other nodes copy its result by digest.
items.label: List refresh interval

items.help: How many answers the cache holds, e.g. 200000; when it is full the least recently used answer is dropped. More entries mean more cache hits and more memory; 0 turns the cache off.
items.label: Maximum cache entries

items.help: Longest time an answer stays cached, even when its record asks for more, e.g. 24h; lower it so changed addresses show up sooner. 0 sets no upper limit.
items.label: Maximum TTL

items.help: Shortest time an answer stays cached, even when its record asks for less, e.g. 5s. Raising it saves upstream queries but keeps changed addresses longer; 0 honors every record's TTL.
items.label: Minimum TTL

items.help: Longest time a "does not exist" answer (NXDOMAIN or NODATA) stays cached, e.g. 5m; shorter lets a newly created name resolve sooner. Below it the zone's SOA minimum applies (RFC 2308).
items.label: Maximum negative TTL

items.help: Refresh popular answers shortly before they expire, so nobody waits for the upstream: an answer asked for this many times within cache.prefetch.window counts as popular, e.g. 5. 0 turns prefetching off.
items.label: Prefetch threshold (hits)

items.help: Time over which the hits for cache.prefetch.threshold are counted, e.g. 2h.
items.label: Prefetch window

items.help: TTL given to an expired answer served this way, e.g. 30s, so clients ask again soon; after a failed refresh, queries for the entry also stop waiting for the upstream for this long. 0 means 30s (RFC 8767).
items.label: Stale answer TTL

items.help: How long a query for an expired entry waits for a fresh upstream answer before the expired one is sent, e.g. 1800ms; 0 means 1800ms (RFC 8767 client response timer).
items.label: Stale answer wait

items.help: When every upstream server fails, keep answering from expired cache entries for up to this long after they expired, e.g. 72h, so names you already use keep working through an outage. 0 turns it off (RFC 8767 serve-stale).
items.label: Serve stale for

items.help: Validate forwarded DNS answers against the configured trust anchors. Invalid or incomplete proofs return SERVFAIL with an extended DNS error; unsigned delegations still work. Off by default for compatibility. A forward zone can override this default with spec.forward.dnssecValidation.
items.label: Validate DNSSEC

items.help: Temporary exceptions for broken signed domains (RFC 7646); at most 128. Every exception needs a reason and an absolute expiry no more than seven days away. It covers the domain and descendants, never sets AD, and stops applying at expiry even on cache hits. Reload and restart do not extend it.

fields.help: Domain whose signatures temporarily cannot be checked, e.g. broken.example; includes its descendants.
fields.label: Domain
fields.name: domain

fields.help: Why validation is temporarily bypassed, in at most 256 characters; record the incident or repair being tracked.
fields.label: Reason
fields.name: reason

fields.help: Absolute RFC3339 expiry, e.g. 2026-10-15T12:00:00Z; no more than seven days from now. Expired entries are harmless and can be removed.
fields.label: Expires at
fields.name: expiresAt

items.label: Temporary validation exceptions

items.help: Additional trusted DS or DNSKEY records in DNS presentation format, e.g. a complete DS record for a private signed zone. At most 64. With useBuiltinAnchors off these replace the shipped root anchors, and at least one is required. Changes invalidate the old validation cache context immediately.
items.label: Additional trust anchors

items.help: Trust the IANA root DS records shipped with this version. Software upgrades or an operator change maintain these anchors; no keys are trusted automatically from upstream responses. Turn off only when dnssec.trustAnchors supplies all trust roots you need.
items.label: Use built-in root trust anchors

items.help: Let external-dns, the Kubernetes tool, publish DNS records into kudurru through its webhook provider protocol (GET /, GET and POST /records, POST /adjustendpoints), served on externalDNS.webhook.listen.
items.label: external-dns webhook enabled

items.help: Address and port of the external-dns webhook, e.g. 127.0.0.1:8888. It has no authentication, so the default answers only on this machine (external-dns as a sidecar or on the same host); a wider address lets every client that reaches it write records. The Helm chart renders :<port> behind its NetworkPolicy.
items.label: external-dns webhook address

items.help: Namespace the record sets from external-dns are stored in, e.g. external-dns: one DNSRecordSet per DNS name, managed by integration:external-dns.
items.label: external-dns record namespace

items.help: Labels a primary zone must carry for external-dns to write into it, e.g. external-dns: enabled (a label selector, key: value); empty allows every primary zone.
items.label: external-dns zone selector

items.help: Address and port of the dashboard and the HTTP API, e.g. 0.0.0.0:8080 for every address or 127.0.0.1:8080 for this machine only; browse to https://<server address>:8080.
items.label: API and UI address

items.help: URL path the dashboard and API are served under when a reverse proxy mounts kudurru below the root of a site, e.g. /kudurru for https://home.example/kudurru/. Empty serves them at /.
items.label: API path prefix

items.help: Whether the dashboard uses HTTPS with a certificate kudurru makes itself when no certificate file is set. selfsigned (default) encrypts the connection, though browsers warn because no public authority signed the certificate; off serves plain HTTP, for use behind a reverse proxy that handles TLS. The certificate is generated once into <node.dataDir>/keys/.
items.label: API automatic TLS

enum.label: Self-signed
enum.help: HTTPS with a certificate generated once into <node.dataDir>/keys/; browsers warn until you trust it.

enum.label: Off (plain HTTP)
enum.help: Plain HTTP, only behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS: otherwise passwords cross the network unencrypted.

items.help: Path of your own certificate for the dashboard (PEM, full chain), e.g. /etc/kudurru/tls/tls.crt; set it with the key file to replace the self-signed certificate. Takes precedence over listeners.api.tls.auto.
items.label: API certificate file

items.help: Path of the private key (PEM) of listeners.api.tls.certFile, e.g. /etc/kudurru/tls/tls.key.
items.label: API key file

items.help: Reverse proxies in front of the dashboard, as addresses or CIDRs, e.g. 192.168.1.5 or 10.0.0.0/8. Only requests from them may report the real client address and scheme in X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto; empty trusts no proxy.
items.label: Trusted reverse proxies

items.help: Address and port where the block page answers browsers over plain HTTP, e.g. :80; empty turns it off. Under the blockPage block response, blocked names point at this server, so a browser that opens one lands here. Needs blockPage.enabled.
items.label: Block page HTTP address

items.help: Optional address and port of the block page over HTTPS, e.g. :443; empty (the default) leaves it off. No certificate can be valid for the blocked names, so browsers show a certificate warning before the page, and sites that use HSTS show no page at all (docs/deploy/blocking-page.md).
items.label: Block page HTTPS address

items.help: Path of the certificate (PEM) of the HTTPS block page. Empty generates a self-signed one into <node.dataDir>/keys/blockpage.crt; a certificate of your own cannot match the blocked names either.
items.label: Block page certificate file

items.help: Path of the private key (PEM) of listeners.blockPage.tls.certFile.
items.label: Block page key file

items.help: Addresses where devices send plain DNS queries. Port 53 is what devices expect; the default 0.0.0.0:53 answers on every address over UDP and TCP. Bind one address, e.g. 192.168.1.10:53, when another service on the machine already uses port 53.
items.label: DNS listeners

fields.name: address
fields.label: Address
fields.help: Address and port to listen on: 0.0.0.0:53, [::]:53 or :53 for every address, or one address such as 192.168.1.10:53.

fields.name: protocols
fields.label: Protocols
fields.help: Transports served on this address: udp, tcp or both. Empty serves both, which is what devices expect.

enum.label: UDP
enum.help: Plain DNS over UDP; what most devices use.

enum.label: TCP
enum.help: Plain DNS over TCP; used for large answers and by clients that retry over TCP.

items.help: Encrypted DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH), usually on port 443, for browsers and devices that support it. Each entry needs an address, e.g. 0.0.0.0:443, a certificate and key, and optionally a path (default /dns-query). Empty serves none. RFC 8484, HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1.
items.label: DNS-over-HTTPS listeners

fields.name: address
fields.label: Address
fields.help: Address and port to listen on: 0.0.0.0:443, [::]:443 or :443 for every address, or one address such as 192.168.1.10:443.

fields.name: path
fields.label: Path
fields.help: URL path of the endpoint, starting with /; empty means /dns-query, what most clients expect.

fields.name: tls
fields.label: TLS
fields.help: Certificate and private key files of this listener.

fields.name: certFile
fields.label: Certificate file
fields.help: Path of the certificate (PEM, full chain), e.g. /etc/kudurru/tls/tls.crt; it must be valid for the name clients use. Reloaded when the file changes.

fields.name: keyFile
fields.label: Key file
fields.help: Path of the private key (PEM) of certFile, e.g. /etc/kudurru/tls/tls.key.

items.help: Encrypted DNS-over-HTTPS over HTTP/3 (QUIC), usually on UDP port 443, for browsers that support it. Each entry needs an address, e.g. 0.0.0.0:443, a certificate and key, and optionally a path (default /dns-query). Empty serves none. ALPN h3.
items.label: DNS-over-HTTP/3 listeners

fields.name: address
fields.label: Address
fields.help: Address and port to listen on: 0.0.0.0:443, [::]:443 or :443 for every address, or one address such as 192.168.1.10:443.

fields.name: path
fields.label: Path
fields.help: URL path of the endpoint, starting with /; empty means /dns-query, what most clients expect.

fields.name: tls
fields.label: TLS
fields.help: Certificate and private key files of this listener.

fields.name: certFile
fields.label: Certificate file
fields.help: Path of the certificate (PEM, full chain), e.g. /etc/kudurru/tls/tls.crt; it must be valid for the name clients use. Reloaded when the file changes.

fields.name: keyFile
fields.label: Key file
fields.help: Path of the private key (PEM) of certFile, e.g. /etc/kudurru/tls/tls.key.

items.help: Encrypted DNS-over-QUIC (DoQ), usually on UDP port 853, for clients that support it. Each entry needs an address, e.g. 0.0.0.0:853, and a certificate and key. Empty serves none. RFC 9250, ALPN doq.
items.label: DNS-over-QUIC listeners

fields.name: address
fields.label: Address
fields.help: Address and port to listen on: 0.0.0.0:853, [::]:853 or :853 for every address, or one address such as 192.168.1.10:853.

fields.name: tls
fields.label: TLS
fields.help: Certificate and private key files of this listener.

fields.name: certFile
fields.label: Certificate file
fields.help: Path of the certificate (PEM, full chain), e.g. /etc/kudurru/tls/tls.crt; it must be valid for the name clients use. Reloaded when the file changes.

fields.name: keyFile
fields.label: Key file
fields.help: Path of the private key (PEM) of certFile, e.g. /etc/kudurru/tls/tls.key.

items.help: Encrypted DNS-over-TLS (DoT), usually on port 853, for devices that support it such as Android's Private DNS. Each entry needs an address, e.g. 0.0.0.0:853, and a certificate and key valid for the name devices use. Empty serves none. RFC 7858, ALPN dot.
items.label: DNS-over-TLS listeners

fields.name: address
fields.label: Address
fields.help: Address and port to listen on: 0.0.0.0:853, [::]:853 or :853 for every address, or one address such as 192.168.1.10:853.

fields.name: tls
fields.label: TLS
fields.help: Certificate and private key files of this listener.

fields.name: certFile
fields.label: Certificate file
fields.help: Path of the certificate (PEM, full chain), e.g. /etc/kudurru/tls/tls.crt; it must be valid for the name clients use. Reloaded when the file changes.

fields.name: keyFile
fields.label: Key file
fields.help: Path of the private key (PEM) of certFile, e.g. /etc/kudurru/tls/tls.key.

items.help: Address and port the other nodes of a cluster use to reach this one, e.g. 0.0.0.0:8082; a single server does not need it reachable. Always TLS with a bearer token; it serves list bodies by digest and /internal/status.
items.label: Node-to-node listener address

items.help: Path of the CA bundle (PEM) trusted when this node connects to other nodes; set it together with your own certificates. Empty trusts the CA derived from the encryption key.
items.label: Internal CA bundle

items.help: Path of the certificate (PEM) of the node-to-node listener, for your own PKI. Empty (the usual choice) issues one from a CA derived from the encryption key, which every node with the same key trusts.
items.label: Internal certificate file

items.help: Path of the private key (PEM) of listeners.internal.tls.certFile.
items.label: Internal key file

items.help: Name checked in other nodes' certificates, e.g. kudurru-internal.home.example; it must be a SAN of listeners.internal.tls.certFile. Empty uses the fixed name of the derived certificates.
items.label: Internal TLS server name

items.help: Path of a file holding the token nodes present to each other. Empty (the usual choice) derives it from the encryption key, so every node with the same KUDURRU_ENCRYPTION_KEY agrees on it (HKDF).
items.label: Internal token file

items.help: Address and port Prometheus scrapes metrics from (/metrics), e.g. 0.0.0.0:9153, or 127.0.0.1:9153 to keep them on this machine.
items.label: Metrics listener address

items.help: Address and port of the health checks Docker, Kubernetes and load balancers poll, e.g. 0.0.0.0:8081 (/healthz/live, /healthz/ready). They need no login.
items.label: Health listener address

items.help: Only with a dnsdist front end: the exact addresses allowed to tell kudurru the real client address in a PROXY protocol v2 header, as CIDRs, normally one /32 per front end, e.g. 192.168.1.2/32. Leave empty when devices query kudurru directly. Use loopback only when dnsdist shares kudurru's network namespace.
items.label: PROXYv2 peers

items.help: Path of a file holding the secret shared with the dnsdist front end, at least 32 bytes, e.g. made with openssl rand -hex 32. Required when proxyProtocolFrom names a peer that is not loopback, so another host cannot forge client addresses. Carried in PROXYv2 TLV 0xE0.
items.label: PROXYv2 secret file

items.help: How many sockets each UDP and TCP DNS listener opens, so several CPU cores read queries in parallel. 0 (default) opens one per CPU (GOMAXPROCS), 1 a single socket. Uses SO_REUSEPORT on Linux, each socket with its own read loop; other systems always use one.
items.label: Sockets per DNS listener

items.help: Format of the log lines: json (default) for log collectors, text for reading in a terminal.
items.label: Log format

enum.label: JSON
enum.help: One JSON object per line; for log collectors.

enum.label: Text
enum.help: key=value lines; easier to read in a terminal.

items.help: How much the server logs: info (default) for normal operation, debug for troubleshooting, warn or error for less. Per-component levels follow a comma, e.g. info,dns=debug.
items.label: Log level

enum.label: Debug
enum.help: Everything, including detail for troubleshooting; noisy.

enum.label: Info
enum.help: Start-up, changes and notable events; the default.

enum.label: Warning
enum.help: Only problems that need attention, and errors.

enum.label: Error
enum.help: Only errors.

items.help: Directory where kudurru keeps its data, e.g. /var/lib/kudurru; it must be writable and should survive restarts and be backed up. It holds the object store (state.db), the query log (querylog.db), the zone snapshot (local.db), downloaded lists and keys.
items.label: Data directory

items.help: How long the server keeps answering after it is told to stop, so devices and load balancers move to another server first, e.g. 2s; 0 stops at once. During this window readiness (/healthz/ready) answers 503 and the health name SERVFAIL, then the listeners close. The Helm chart also runs kudurru lameduck in preStop.
items.label: Lameduck drain window

items.help: Name of this server in the dashboard, the query log and the block page, e.g. dns1. Empty uses the hostname. Every node of a cluster needs its own name; it identifies the node to the others.
items.label: Node name

items.help: Local IP address that NOTIFY messages to secondary servers are sent from, e.g. 192.168.1.10; empty lets the system choose. Secondaries accept NOTIFY only from an address they list as a primary.
items.label: NOTIFY source address

items.help: Zones, lists, groups and policies declared in this file, in the form of Kubernetes manifests (apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec). They are re-applied on every start; edit them here, since they are managed by file:kudurru.yaml and the dashboard cannot change them.
items.label: Inline objects

fields.name: apiVersion
fields.label: API version
fields.help: API version of the object, e.g. kudurru.io/v1alpha1.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind
fields.help: Kind of the object, e.g. DNSZone, DNSRecordSet, BlockList, ClientGroup or Policy.

fields.name: metadata
fields.label: Metadata
fields.help: Object metadata: the name, and optionally labels, as in a Kubernetes manifest.

fields.name: spec
fields.label: Spec
fields.help: The object's settings, as described for its kind in the CRD reference.

items.help: Directory of *.yaml files with zones, lists, groups and policies, e.g. /etc/kudurru/objects.d. It is watched: adding or editing a file applies it, and deleting a document deletes the object. The objects are managed by file:<dir>/<name>, so the dashboard cannot change them.
items.label: Objects directory

items.help: How client addresses are hidden under the anonymize_client privacy mode: prefix keeps only the network (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48), so devices in one network look alike; pseudonym replaces each address with a code that is stable for a day and cannot be reversed.
items.label: Client anonymization

enum.label: Prefix
enum.help: Keep only the network of each address: IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48.

enum.label: Pseudonym
enum.help: Replace each address with a code that stays the same for a day and cannot be reversed (HMAC with a random in-memory key rotated daily, so codes also change on restart).

items.help: Record the queries each node answers, for the dashboard's query log, statistics and charts; off stops new recording and preserves earlier local history. Each node keeps its own log (querylog.db with rollups, the stats API).
items.label: Query log enabled

items.help: Clients whose queries are never logged, e.g. 192.168.1.20, 10.0.0.0/8 or a client name such as nas: IP addresses, CIDR prefixes or client names.
items.label: Clients never logged

items.help: Names that are never logged, e.g. *.home.arpa or connectivitycheck.gstatic.com: exact names, *.suffix for a domain and everything below it, or /regex/.
items.label: Domains never logged

items.help: Leave out names that never leave the local network, which keeps local discovery noise out of the log: localhost, .local, .home.arpa and private and link-local reverse zones (special-use names, RFC 6761).
items.label: Skip special-use names

items.help: How much of each query is kept: full keeps everything; the other modes hide client addresses, query names or both, and nothing keeps only per-minute totals. Applied once when the query is recorded, so it cannot be undone for queries already logged. Only full stores the answer summary.
items.label: Query log privacy

enum.label: Full
enum.help: Keep the client, the name and the answer summary of every query.

enum.label: Anonymize clients
enum.help: Keep the names but hide client addresses, as set by querylog.anonymize.

enum.label: Hide domains
enum.help: Keep the clients but not the names they asked for.

enum.label: Hide domains and clients
enum.help: Keep neither names nor clients.

enum.label: Totals only
enum.help: Keep no rows, only per-minute totals for the charts.

items.help: Largest size of the query log database on each node, e.g. 10GiB; when it is exceeded the oldest queries are deleted first. 0 removes the cap.
items.label: Maximum query log size

items.help: How long individual queries are kept, e.g. 720h (30 days); 0 keeps them until querylog.retention.maxDBBytes is reached. The totals behind the charts are kept longer: per minute for 35 days, per hour for 400 days, per day forever.
items.label: Keep query rows for

items.help: Where queries are recorded: sqlite (default) keeps them in a database the dashboard reads; slog writes one JSON log line per query without adding database rows, for an external log system.
items.label: Query log sink

enum.label: SQLite
enum.help: A database on each node (querylog.db, with rollups); needed for the dashboard's query log and statistics.

enum.label: Log lines
enum.help: One JSON log line per query; earlier local history remains readable.

items.help: Limit how many queries per minute one address or network may send over UDP, which blunts floods and reflection attacks. TCP, DoT, DoH, DoQ and DoH3 are never limited, nor loopback clients and the health name.
items.label: Rate limiting enabled

items.help: Addresses or networks that are never rate limited, e.g. 192.168.1.0/24 for your LAN or the address of a busy resolver that forwards to kudurru. Loopback always is.
items.label: Exempt clients

items.help: Queries per minute allowed per IPv4 address or network, by prefix length: 32 is one address (default 600), 24 a /24 network (default 6000). Entries merge with the defaults key by key, and 0 turns a level off. Each prefix has a token bucket holding one minute's allowance.
items.label: IPv4 limits (queries per minute)

items.help: Queries per minute allowed per IPv6 address or network, by prefix length: 128 is one address (default 600), 64 a /64 network (6000), 56 a /56 (12000). Entries merge with the defaults key by key, and 0 turns a level off.
items.label: IPv6 limits (queries per minute)

items.help: Most addresses and networks tracked at once, e.g. 65536 (0 means 65536); the least recently seen is forgotten first and starts again with a full allowance.
items.label: Tracked prefixes

items.help: Share of over-limit queries, in percent from 0 to 100, answered with an empty truncated reply (TC=1) instead of being dropped, e.g. 50; real clients then retry over TCP, which is not limited. 0 drops them all, 100 answers them all.
items.label: Slip (percent answered TC=1)

items.help: Who may do what: each binding grants a role (viewer, auditor, operator, zone-admin or admin) to users, groups or service accounts, for the whole cluster or one zone. RoleBinding objects add to these.
items.label: Role bindings

fields.name: role
fields.label: Role
fields.help: Role granted to the subjects.

enum.label: Viewer
enum.help: Read zones, records, lists, policies, clients, stats and settings; change nothing.

enum.label: Auditor
enum.help: Viewer plus reading the query log, the audit log and unblock requests.

enum.label: Operator
enum.help: Day-to-day blocking work: manage records, lists, policies, client groups, clients and unblock requests, toggle blocking and flush the cache. No zones, users or settings.

enum.label: Zone admin
enum.help: Manage zones and their records, transfers and signing; bind it to a zone scope.

enum.label: Admin
enum.help: Everything, including users, role bindings and settings.

fields.name: scope
fields.label: Scope
fields.help: Where the role applies; empty means the whole cluster.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind
fields.help: What the role is limited to: the whole cluster, one zone, a zone group or a client group.

enum.label: Cluster
enum.help: The role applies everywhere.

enum.label: Zone
enum.help: The role applies to the zone named in scope.name.

enum.label: Zone group
enum.help: The role applies to the zone group named in scope.name (reserved: zone groups arrive in v0.2).

enum.label: Client group
enum.help: The role applies to the client group named in scope.name (reserved for v1.0).

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.help: Zone, zone group or client group name, e.g. home.example; empty for cluster scope.

fields.name: subjects
fields.label: Subjects
fields.help: Who gets the role: users, groups or service accounts; at least one.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind
fields.help: Whether name is a user, a group or a service account.

enum.label: User
enum.help: One account by username: a local user (e.g. alice) or an identity-provider login (e.g. corp:alice).

enum.label: Group
enum.help: Every member of a group, e.g. a local group or an identity-provider group such as corp:/dns-admins.

enum.label: Service account
enum.help: A kudurru or Kubernetes service account, by name and namespace.

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.help: Username, group or service-account name, e.g. alice, corp:alice or corp:/dns-admins; names from an identity provider carry its id as a prefix.

fields.name: namespace
fields.label: Namespace
fields.help: Namespace of the service account, e.g. kudurru; required for a ServiceAccount, empty for users and groups.

items.help: Path of a file for the cluster-wide settings, e.g. /etc/kudurru/settings.yaml, read on top of this file and watched, so edits apply without a restart. In Docker, changes made on the Settings page are saved into it; without one they are lost on restart. KUDURRU_SETTINGS_FILE takes precedence, and the Helm chart mounts /etc/kudurru/settings/settings.yaml. Empty turns the layer off (D25).
items.label: Settings file

items.help: Where kudurru keeps its objects (zones, lists, policies, users): sqlite, a database file under node.dataDir, for Docker and single servers; kube, Kubernetes custom resources, which the Helm chart sets.
items.label: Store driver

enum.label: SQLite
enum.help: A database file (state.db) under node.dataDir; for Docker and single servers.

enum.label: Kubernetes
enum.help: Kubernetes custom resources (CRDs) through the apiserver; what the Helm chart uses.

items.help: Kubernetes only: the oldest saved copy (local.db) the node may answer its own zones from while the apiserver is unreachable, e.g. 24h. An older copy is not trusted: the node reports not ready and its primary zones answer SERVFAIL.
items.label: Snapshot maximum age

items.help: Kubernetes only: how long to wait at start for the apiserver to deliver the objects, e.g. 15s. After that the node answers from its last saved copy (local.db) until the apiserver catches up.
items.label: Kubernetes sync timeout

items.help: Shared keys that authenticate zone transfers and NOTIFY between kudurru and other DNS servers; only needed when you transfer zones. Each key has a name, an algorithm and a file holding the secret, and a zone lists the keys it accepts in spec.policy.transferTSIGKeyRefs (TSIG, RFC 8945).
items.label: TSIG keys

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.help: Name of the key, a domain name such as xfr.home.example; the other server must use the same name, and zones list it in spec.policy.transferTSIGKeyRefs.

fields.name: algorithm
fields.label: Algorithm
fields.help: HMAC algorithm of the key; it must match the other server.

enum.label: HMAC-SHA256
enum.help: The common choice; every current DNS server supports it.

enum.label: HMAC-SHA512
enum.help: A longer digest; use it when the other server requires it.

fields.name: secretFile
fields.label: Secret file
fields.help: Path of a file holding only the base64 secret, e.g. /etc/kudurru/xfr.key: the quoted value of the secret line tsig-keygen prints, or the output of openssl rand -base64 32.

items.help: Let people ask for a blocked site to be unblocked: the block page shows a Request access form, and requests appear on the dashboard's Requests page for an administrator to approve or deny. Needs blockPage.enabled.
items.label: Unblock requests

items.help: Most undecided unblock requests kept across the cluster, e.g. 1000. When reached, the block page says requests are paused until an administrator decides some.
items.label: Most pending unblock requests

items.help: Undecided unblock requests expire after this long, e.g. 336h (14 days); at least 1h.
items.label: Pending requests expire after

items.help: Most unblock requests one client may send per hour, e.g. 5; IPv6 clients are counted per /64. Asking again for the same name updates the pending request instead of adding one.
items.label: Unblock requests per hour per client

items.help: How long decided and expired unblock requests stay on the Requests page, counted from the decision, e.g. 720h (30 days); at least 1h. A time-limited approval is kept until it ends.
items.label: Keep decided requests for

items.help: Plain DNS servers used only to look up the host names of upstream servers, such as dns.quad9.net in tls://dns.quad9.net, e.g. 1.1.1.1:53 or 9.9.9.9. Never asked for client queries.
items.label: Bootstrap resolvers

items.help: Send queries for some domains to a chosen upstream group, e.g. home.lan to a group holding your router, so local device names resolve. Each entry maps a domain suffix to a group name; the longest matching suffix wins, and a key may list several suffixes in dnsmasq form, "[/corp.example/10.in-addr.arpa/]". These answers are never cached.
items.label: Conditional forwarding

items.help: How much of an IPv4 client address EDNS Client Subnet may reveal, as a prefix length from 0 to 32: with 24 (default) only the network, e.g. 203.0.113.0/24, is sent. Used only when upstreams.ecs.mode is forward or add.
items.label: ECS IPv4 prefix length

items.help: How much of an IPv6 client address EDNS Client Subnet may reveal, as a prefix length from 0 to 128: with 56 (default) only the /56 network is sent. Used only when upstreams.ecs.mode is forward or add.
items.label: ECS IPv6 prefix length

items.help: Whether upstream servers learn which network a query came from (EDNS Client Subnet). strip (default) never tells them, the private choice; forward and add can get answers from servers nearer the client, at the cost of revealing part of its address.
items.label: EDNS Client Subnet

enum.label: Strip
enum.help: Never send a client subnet upstream; the private choice and the default.

enum.label: Forward
enum.help: Pass on a subnet the client sent itself, shortened to the prefix lengths below.

enum.label: Add
enum.help: Like Forward, and add a subnet for clients with a public address that sent none.

items.help: The DNS servers kudurru asks for names it does not answer itself, in named groups; the group named default gets every query nothing else routes. Each group lists servers (e.g. 1.1.1.1, tls://dns.quad9.net), a strategy that picks among them and a timeout per server. Conditional forwarding, forward zones and policies send queries to other groups by name.
items.label: Upstream groups

fields.name: mode
fields.label: Mode
fields.help: forward (default) sends queries to the servers below; recursive resolves names itself from the root servers, so no single provider sees every name, and validates DNSSEC (see upstreams.recursion).

enum.label: Forward
enum.help: Send queries to the servers you list, such as your ISP, Cloudflare or Quad9.

enum.label: Recursive
enum.help: Resolve names from the root servers with kudurru's own resolver and validate DNSSEC; no single provider sees every name.

fields.name: servers
fields.label: Servers
fields.help: DNS servers this group forwards to, e.g. 1.1.1.1, tls://dns.quad9.net or https://dns.google/dns-query. A bare address uses plain DNS on port 53; tls://, https://, quic://, h3:// and sdns:// stamps encrypt the queries. Prefix a display name with name=, e.g. cloudflare=tls://1.1.1.1. Required in forward mode; a recursive group has none.

fields.name: strategy
fields.label: Strategy
fields.help: How the servers are picked for each query; parallel_best suits most setups. Forward mode only.

enum.label: Parallel best
enum.help: Ask two healthy servers picked at random at once and use the first good answer; if both fail, ask the rest. Fast and resilient; suits most setups.

enum.label: Strict order
enum.help: Ask the servers one at a time in the listed order, moving to the next only when one fails. Use it when the first server should answer whenever it can.

enum.label: Random
enum.help: Ask one healthy server picked at random, and another random one if it fails. Spreads the load evenly.

enum.label: Fastest (RTT weighted)
enum.help: Prefer the servers that answer fastest: the first is picked at random weighted by its inverse round-trip time, then the rest are tried in RTT order.

fields.name: timeout
fields.label: Timeout
fields.help: How long to wait for one server's answer before trying another, e.g. 2s; raise it for slow or distant servers. In recursive mode it bounds the whole lookup of a name (default 4s).

items.help: Check DNSSEC signatures on answers from recursive groups, from the root trust anchors down. Forged or broken answers in signed zones become SERVFAIL (status dnssec_bogus) instead of reaching devices; unsigned zones still resolve. Clients that set the CD bit get the data anyway.
items.label: DNSSEC validation

items.help: Whether recursive groups ask name servers over IPv6. auto (default) does when this host has an IPv6 route to the root servers.
items.label: IPv6 to name servers

enum.label: Auto
enum.help: Use IPv6 when the host has an IPv6 route to the root servers.

enum.label: On
enum.help: Always ask IPv6 name servers too.

enum.label: Off
enum.help: Ask name servers over IPv4 only.

items.help: Send each name server only as much of the name as it needs (QNAME minimization, RFC 9156): the root servers learn com, not www.example.com. Recursive groups only.
items.label: QNAME minimization

items.help: Addresses of the root servers recursive groups start from, e.g. 198.41.0.4; empty (the default) uses the built-in IANA list. Only for a private root or a lab: with custom hints, name servers on private and link-local addresses are asked too, which the public tree never allows.
items.label: Root hints

items.help: Root DS records DNSSEC validation trusts, e.g. 20326 8 2 E06D44B8...; empty (the default) uses the built-in KSK-2017 and KSK-2024 anchors from IANA. Only for a root key rollover the built-in list does not know yet, or for a private root.
items.label: Root trust anchors

items.help: Client prefixes allowed to query; empty uses private and loopback ranges.
items.label: Edge acl

items.help: Loopback-only dnsdist webserver/API address.
items.label: Edge api

items.help: Group name or GID for apiKeyOut; empty preserves the file group.
items.label: Edge api-key-group

items.help: Write the random per-start API key to this host file with mode 0640; empty does not write a key file.
items.label: Edge api-key-out

items.help: Cache the authoritative pool briefly and invalidate on zone serial changes.
items.label: Edge authoritative-cache

items.help: Maximum authoritative cache TTL in seconds.
items.label: Edge authoritative-cache-ttl

items.help: Zones routed to the authoritative pool in addition to zones polled from backends.
items.label: Edge authoritative-zones

items.help: DNS backend port when no port is specified.
items.label: Edge backend-port

items.help: EndpointSlice port name carrying DNS.
items.label: Edge backend-port-name

items.help: Static [name=]host[:port] backends. Every edge lists every Kudurru node; empty requires a membership source.
items.label: Edge backends

items.help: Membership source: static or endpointslice:<namespace>/<service>.
items.label: Edge backends-from

items.help: Resolver packet-cache entries; zero uses the renderer default.
items.label: Edge cache-size

items.help: Directory for configuration rendered by edge run.
items.label: Edge config-dir

items.help: Loopback-only dnsdist console address.
items.label: Edge console

items.help: Delay before rerendering membership or certificate changes.
items.label: Edge debounce

items.help: dnsdist executable used by edge run.
items.label: Edge dnsdist-bin

items.help: uid[:gid] dnsdist switches to after binding sockets; empty retains the current user.
items.label: Edge dnsdist-user

items.help: Explicit doh frontend host:port, using a listen address. Requires TLS files.
items.label: Edge doh

items.help: Explicit doh3 frontend host:port, using a listen address. Requires TLS files.
items.label: Edge doh3

items.help: Explicit doq frontend host:port, using a listen address. Requires TLS files.
items.label: Edge doq

items.help: Explicit dot frontend host:port, using a listen address. Requires TLS files.
items.label: Edge dot

items.help: Readiness refusal period before restarting dnsdist.
items.label: Edge drain

items.help: Enable dnsdist dynamic blocking.
items.label: Edge dynblocks

items.help: Per-client NXDOMAIN rate that triggers a dynamic block; zero disables it.
items.label: Edge dynblocks-nxdomain-rate

items.help: Per-client query rate over ten seconds that triggers a dynamic block.
items.label: Edge dynblocks-qps

items.help: Use an eBPF socket filter for dynamic-block drops; requires host capabilities.
items.label: Edge ebpf

items.help: Supervisor health, status and metrics listener used by edge run.
items.label: Edge health-address

items.help: Host CA file for backend internal TLS; empty derives it from the encryption key.
items.label: Edge internal-ca-file

items.help: Backend internal listener port for zone serial polling; zero disables it.
items.label: Edge internal-port

items.help: Backend internal TLS server name; empty uses internal.kudurru.invalid.
items.label: Edge internal-server-name

items.help: Host file with the internal bearer token; empty derives it from the encryption key.
items.label: Edge internal-token-file

items.help: IP addresses every frontend binds.
items.label: Edge listen

items.help: Resolver pool load-balancing policy, validated by the existing renderer.
items.label: Edge pool-resolver

items.help: Do53 listener threads; zero uses the renderer default.
items.label: Edge threads

items.help: TLS certificate directory. Supports tls.crt/tls.key, fullchain.pem/privkey.pem or cert.pem/key.pem; watched for rotation.
items.label: Edge tls-dir

items.label: VIP hmac-key-file

items.label: VIP keepalived-bin

items.label: VIP kudurru-bin

items.help: Render for keepalived 2.3 without auth_hmac; VRRP advertisements are unauthenticated.

items.help: Supervisor logging level for vip run.
items.label: VIP log-level

items.help: Node count; zero uses peers plus one.
items.label: VIP node-count

items.help: Other nodes unicast addresses.
items.label: VIP peers

items.help: Host file containing one peer address per line; overrides peers and is watched by vip run.
items.label: VIP peers-file

items.help: nodes:<selector> discovers Kubernetes Node InternalIPs; cannot be combined with peers or peersFile.
items.label: VIP peers-from

items.help: Per-VIP preemption delay in seconds; empty uses nopreempt. Environment accepts a JSON object.
items.label: VIP preempt-delay

values.help: Preemption delay in seconds, zero uses nopreempt.

items.help: Node priority index. With Node discovery, an omitted value uses this node position; explicitly configured zero remains zero.
items.label: VIP priority-index

items.help: Whitespace-separated command prefix for the existing VRRP probe script; shell syntax is not evaluated.
items.label: VIP probe-command

items.label: VIP unicast-src

items.help: Host VIP records. VRIDs are explicitly assigned by the operator and never allocated remotely. Environment accepts a JSON array.

fields.name: name

fields.help: VIP address with prefix length, for example 192.0.2.53/24.
fields.label: Address
fields.name: address

fields.help: Host interface receiving the VIP address.
fields.label: Interface
fields.name: interface

fields.help: Operator-assigned virtual router ID, unique on this host; never allocated by an API write.
fields.label: VRID
fields.name: vrid

items.label: VIP vip

items.help: Interface for VRRP advertisements; empty uses each VIP interface.
items.label: VIP vrrp-interface

items.help: Namespace containing MetalLB ServiceL2Status and speaker Pods. Requires read permissions; at most 64 status objects per acquisition. No provider credential or write permission is added.
items.label: MetalLB announcer namespace

items.help: Read-only polling interval, 1s-1m. Polling does not renew a provider heartbeat.
items.label: VIP observation interval

items.help: Local acquisition expiry measured from its original start; at least interval+timeout, at most 1m. Provider Lease or Node heartbeat expiry can shorten this; a fresh L2 status read never invents a provider heartbeat.
items.label: VIP observation maximum age

items.help: Read-only ownership evidence in serve; never starts or controls a supervisor. kube-vip supports per-Service ARP leader Leases; MetalLB supports L2 status with live matching speaker and Node. BGP/global/ambiguous sources remain unknown.
items.label: VIP observation provider

enum.label: Disabled
enum.help: Do not acquire VIP ownership evidence.

enum.label: kube-vip
enum.help: Observe per-Service kubevip-<service> Leases agreeing with vipHost, assigned IP and a live Node.

enum.label: MetalLB L2
enum.help: Observe ServiceL2Status, live UID-matching speaker Pod and live Node heartbeat. L2 status has no provider heartbeat or physical ARP proof.

enum.label: Keepalived notifications
enum.help: Read the local Consumer transition journal for audit/live events. Requires vip.vips mappings and a readable observation runDir. No current ownership or writer authority is inferred.

items.help: Up to 32 exact Service/address bindings. File-only structured input; each Service must remain allocated to the expected address. Allocation never implies an owner.
items.label: Observed VIP Services

fields.name: name
fields.label: VIP name
fields.help: Local name for this observed VIP.

fields.name: address
fields.label: Address
fields.help: Expected Service LoadBalancer IP, used only to match allocation, never to infer ownership.

fields.name: namespace
fields.label: Service namespace
fields.help: Exact namespace of the observed Service.

fields.name: service
fields.label: Service name
fields.help: Exact Service name. kube-vip observation requires its per-Service kubevip-<name> Lease.

items.help: Deadline for the entire acquisition, 100ms-5s. Failed reads replace previous ownership with unknown.
items.label: VIP acquisition timeout

items.help: Acquire client names asynchronously from explicit DNS sources. Untrusted fallback only when inventory and DHCP have no name.
items.label: Enable reverse PTR

items.help: Positive lifetime cap, 1s-1h, bounded by DNS TTL from acquisition start. Expired names never remain a fallback.
items.label: PTR maximum age

items.help: Bounded observation cache. Cold and expired names return immediately without waiting for DNS.
items.label: PTR cache entries

items.help: Negative or failed acquisition backoff, 1s-5m. No client name is retained on failure.
items.label: PTR retry delay

items.help: One to 32 explicit IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs eligible for background name acquisition.
items.label: PTR client networks

items.help: One to four explicit unicast IP:port sources. UDP only; no system resolver, DNS search, TCP fallback or CNAME chasing.
items.label: PTR DNS servers

items.help: Original acquisition deadline, 100ms-5s across all configured sources.
items.label: PTR timeout

items.help: Fixed number of background DNS workers. Demand queue holds at most 256 addresses.
items.label: PTR workers

items.help: Absolute directory containing the existing keepalived Consumer journal. Read-only in serve; no FIFO reader, supervisor, weight file or writer is started. Files retain private 0600 access; the serve process must already have permission.
items.label: VIP observation directory
